jobs.title: Design codex — RFC 0053 Phase B schema rename
jobs.objective: Design the workflow.v1.2 schema bump. Required answers (one each): (1) The dual-name read discipline — accept both `human_checkpoint` and `escalation_checkpoint` on parse (with deprecation warning on old name) for one schema generation; write only the new name. Same for `waiting_human` → `waiting_escalation`. Cite src/striatum/workflow.py lines. (2) `workflow upgrade <path>` rule that rewrites v1 fields to v1.2 + bumps schema_version. Cite the existing upgrade infrastructure in src/striatum/cli/workflow.py. (3) Migration for in-flight PG state — any existing `runs.state = 'waiting_human'` rows need to be readable but new transitions write the new name. Cite the runs state column type / check constraint in src/striatum/daemon_pg/sql/. (4) CLI prompt-string sweep target list: src/striatum/cli/recovery.py (checkpoint resolve prompts), src/striatum/cli/parser.py (--severity choices), src/striatum/cli/list_commands.py (state filter), src/striatum/cli/introspect.py (status/why text). Justify which strings rename and which stay (e.g., `--severity` value names rename in v1.2 workflows; the CLI flag itself stays). (5) `escalation` artifact-kind scope — define here, or defer to a follow-up dogfood (064)? Pick one and justify scope. (6) Back-compat tests: a v1 workflow validates with deprecation warning; the same workflow after `workflow upgrade` validates without warnings; both produce identical runtime behavior. (7) New schema-rename audit row format — when the validator emits the deprecation warning, an audit row records it for telemetry.

jobs.title: Review design codex threat_model
jobs.objective: Migration safety + back-compat threat model: (1) Existing v1 workflows in `docs/dogfood/*` must validate after the rename — bounce on any that break. (2) The dual-name read discipline must accept old names everywhere they appear today — bounce on partial coverage. (3) The PG `waiting_human` → `waiting_escalation` transition must not silently lose audit-chain anchors; the rename happens in code, not in a SQL migration that rewrites historical rows. (4) The CLI prompt-string sweep must not change any flag NAMES (operator scripts depend on them); only stderr/help text changes. (5) `workflow upgrade` is idempotent.

jobs.objective: Threat model: dual-name discipline applied everywhere old name appears; PG state-name acceptance doesn't break the existing audit chain (no SQL UPDATE of historical rows); workflow upgrade is idempotent (running it twice produces identical output); no flag NAMES changed (only stderr/help text).

jobs.title: Build review gemini adversarial
jobs.objective: Adversarial: a workflow with BOTH old and new names for the same field (which wins?); a workflow upgrade that loses comments or formatting (json doesn't have comments but check escape semantics); a runtime where new code writes 'waiting_escalation' but legacy reads expect 'waiting_human' (does the dual-read produce stale states?); an operator script that greps for 'human_checkpoint' in `striatum status --json` output and breaks silently.
